name: Tux
kurzbeschreibung: Mountain village in the Tuxertal with the Hintertuxer Gletscher – the only year-round ski area in Tirol and a paradise for nature lovers.
beschreibung:
Overview

Tux is located in the upper Zillertal within the dramatic Tuxertal, a high alpine valley branching southwest from Mayrhofen up to the formidable Hintertux Glacier. Framed by majestic peaks of the Zillertal and Tux Alps—including the soaring Mount Olperer at 3,476 meters—the mountain municipality spans from 1,281 meters in Vorderlanersbach through Lanersbach, Juns, and Madseit to 1,500 meters in Hintertux, with municipal boundaries climbing up to 3,250 meters into the glaciated terrain. Home to around 1,950 inhabitants, Tux is internationally celebrated for uniting rugged high-altitude topography, premier winter sports, and enduring alpine pastoral customs. Hosting Austria's only year-round ski resort, Tux captivates visitors with extraordinary natural phenomena above and below the mountain surface.

History

Stone Age artifacts unearthed at the Tuxer Joch pass indicate that this alpine crossing served as an essential mountain route linking the Zillertal and Wipptal valleys as early as 3,500 years ago. The village was first documented in 1280 as 'Tukches', a pre-Roman name evoking rushing torrents. Up until the 20th century, mountain agriculture and mining—such as magnesite extraction on the Schrofenalm—shaped daily life. A standout cultural monument is the Mehlerhaus in Madseit: this traditional timber double-farmstead dates back to the early 16th century with inscribed beams from 1674. Following meticulous restoration, it now houses a heritage museum featuring an authentic smokehouse kitchen and exhibits illustrating traditional rural life. In Lanersbach, the Parish Church of Saint Thomas was consecrated in Late Gothic style in 1471 and redesigned with Baroque vaults by master Georg Sieberer in 1686, retaining its original medieval spire.

Getting There

By car, travel via the Inntal Autobahn A12 to the Wiesing/Zillertal exit, following the B169 through the Zillertal to Mayrhofen. From Mayrhofen, the scenic Tuxer Landesstraße L6 winds uphill through Finkenberg for approximately 15 kilometers to Hintertux; proper winter equipment is essential during snowy months. Rail passengers take ÖBB trains to Jenbach, transfer to the narrow-gauge Zillertalbahn to Mayrhofen, and board VVT regional bus line 4104 connecting all Tux hamlets to the glacier lift.

Tips

The premier highlight is the Hintertux Glacier, offering skiing 365 days a year across up to 60 kilometers of slopes and a panoramic platform at 3,250 meters. Deep inside the glacier lies the Nature's Ice Palace (Natur Eis Palast), an extraordinary subglacial cave network displaying towering ice crystals and a subterranean glacial lake that can be navigated on stand-up paddleboards. Nearby lies the Spannagel Cave, the highest accessible show cave in Europe and the Central Alps' largest natural marble cavern. In summer, hike across the historic Tuxer Joch pass or tour the folk museum at the Mehlerhaus in Madseit.
